# rabbitsfoot

> rabbitsfoot is an independent product design and UX studio based in Bengaluru,
> India, working worldwide. Seven senior specialists design interfaces for
> environments where being wrong is expensive: counter-drone command and control,
> drone fleet operations, defence logistics, clinical data platforms and
> national-scale enterprise operations.

## What the studio does

- **Product & UX design** — End-to-end digital product design, from research through shipped interface.
- **Mission-critical systems design** — Interfaces for defence, operations and safety-critical environments.
- **Design research** — Field research, usability testing and domain immersion.
- **Industrial design** — Physical products, hardware and device interaction.
- **Spatial & retail experience** — Physical environments, retail and exhibition design.
- **Design systems** — Component libraries, patterns and governance for scaling teams.

## How it differs from a typical UI/UX agency

- Seven senior people, no juniors staffed onto client work and no hand-offs
  in thinking: the people in the pitch are the people who do the work.
- Domain-first. The studio learns the operational domain — ordnance accountability,
  airspace deconfliction, clinical hand-over — before drawing interfaces.
- Works across digital, industrial and spatial design in one team, which is rare for
  a studio of this size.

## Selected work

- [PRAHARI — Counter-Drone Command Interface](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/prahari): Designing a counter-drone command and control interface: threat classification, engagement decisions and operator load under time pressure.
- [Rojnica — Drone Fleet Management](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/rojnica): A fleet management interface for autonomous drones: mission planning, live telemetry and fleet health across many aircraft.
- [Chargeur — Ammunition Load Management](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/chargeur): Ammunition load management for defence logistics: tracking, allocation and accountability of ordnance across units.
- [VIGIL — A Rugged Squad Wearable](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/vigil): A rugged smartwatch and companion system for soldiers in darkness, rain and poor connectivity. Physical controls, haptics and glanceable alerts usable with gloves on.
- [Muspell — Clinical Intelligence Platform](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/muspell): Turning long, fragmented patient records into a clear view of what changed and what care teams should do next.
- [Penknife — Healthcare Staffing Platform](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/penknife): One hiring platform replacing four disconnected tools, so recruiters, managers and candidates move from an open role to a filled shift without losing context.
- [Parkbeheer NL — National Parking Operations](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/parkbeheer): An operations platform for teams managing 923,000 parking spaces across the Netherlands, replacing spreadsheets with one shared workflow for patrols and field work.
- [KLu POS — Point of Sale for Defence Canteens](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/klu-pos): A point-of-sale system built for military canteens rather than restaurants: different stock, different rules, different people behind the counter.
- [Titan EyeX — Smart Eyewear Ecosystem](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/titan-eyex): Designing a smart-eyewear ecosystem for Titan: hardware interaction, companion app and the system connecting them.
- [Titan Eyeplus — Designing Confidence into Eyewear Commerce](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/titan-eyeplus): End-to-end e-commerce redesign for Titan’s optical brand: product discovery, virtual try-on, checkout and repeat purchase.

## Interactive demos

- [PRAHARI — C-UAS Command & Control (Interactive Demo)](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/prahari-app): A playable demo of the PRAHARI counter-drone command and control interface: track classification, threat prioritisation and engagement flow.
- [Rojnica — Swarm Mission Planner (Interactive Demo)](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/rojnica-app): A playable demo of the Rojnica swarm mission planner: routing, deconfliction and live fleet telemetry across many drones.
- [Chargeur — Ammunition State (Interactive Demo)](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/chargeur-app): A playable demo of the Chargeur ammunition state interface: what is in the breech, what the fire order asked for, and how the mismatch is caught.
- [Parkbeheer NL — Car Park Management (Interactive Demo)](https://www.rabbitsfoot.in/parkbeheer-app): A playable demo of the Parkbeheer operations interface: patrol planning, field records and mismatch resolution across national parking stock.

## Frequently asked

### What kind of work does rabbitsfoot take on?

Product and UX design is our deepest practice — digital products taken end to end, from research and product strategy through interaction, interface and build support. Around that we work in design research, design systems, industrial design and spatial and retail experience. The through-line is not the medium. It is problems where being wrong is expensive.

### Do you work on defence and other confidential programmes?

Yes. A significant part of the studio's work is mission-critical: counter-drone command and control, drone fleet operations, ammunition and defence logistics, and rugged wearables for the field. That work reaches us through partner agencies and is covered by NDA, so names, programme details and some numbers are altered in the public case studies. The design decisions and the reasoning behind them are described accurately.

### Where are you based, and can you work with a team elsewhere?

The studio is in Bengaluru, India, and works worldwide. Most of our clients sit three to nine hours behind us, which in practice means a working overlap every afternoon and a finished piece of thinking waiting when your day starts.

### Who actually does the work?

The people in the first call. The studio is deliberately small and entirely senior — no juniors staffed onto client work, no hand-off between the people who understood the problem and the people who draw the answer. That is the reason we stay this size.

### How do you scope and price an engagement?

Nothing is priced before the problem is understood. A thirty-minute call, then a short written response with what we think the real problem is and how we would scope it — usually within a week. Engagements are quoted as a whole piece of work rather than by the hour, so the estimate does not move because a question took longer to answer than expected.

### Can you work alongside our in-house design team?

Often that is the better arrangement. We are used to joining an existing team on the hard part — the system nobody has managed to untangle, the domain that takes months to learn, the design system that needs governance before it needs components — and leaving behind something the in-house team can carry on with.

### Do you design physical products and spaces as well as software?

Yes, and in the same team rather than through a subcontractor. Industrial design and spatial and retail experience sit inside the studio, which is unusual at this size. It matters when a brief crosses over — a wearable that is a device and an interface and a charging story, or a retail journey that is a space and an app at once.

### How quickly will you reply?

Within one working day, from a real person who read what you sent. Half-formed is fine — a screenshot of the spreadsheet everyone actually uses is often the most useful thing you can send.
